extra.message: Passwords are hashed with a single unsalted SHA-256 computation (peppered only with the hardcoded shared APP_SECRET): SHA256(secret + password + secret). SHA-256 is a fast general-purpose hash with no per-user salt and no key stretching, so password_hash values (exposed via the unauthenticated GET /user/all endpoint) can be brute-forced offline at billions of guesses per second once APP_SECRET is known. A slow, salted KDF such as bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2 is required for password storage.

extra.message: The session cookie is set with the option 'expire', which is not a valid Express/cookie option (the correct options are 'expires' or 'maxAge') and is therefore silently ignored, so the intended 1-hour expiry is never applied to the cookie. In addition, the server never expires session_id values (they persist in the users table until explicit logout) and login (user.js line 97) reuses the existing session_id instead of rotating it. As a result, a stolen session cookie remains valid indefinitely.
